metadata.title: Example Sensor Gateway System Security Plan (draft)

system-characteristics.description: The system gives the installation security operations center a near-real-time picture of perimeter intrusion and environmental conditions at remote sites . It senses and forwards only: it makes no decisions and actuates nothing . It is under development, with twelve pre-production units at test sites and 60 units to be fielded after an authorization decision .

information-types.title: Perimeter and environmental sensor telemetry and alarms
information-types.description: Intrusion, door, temperature, water and power readings and alarms with site and sensor identifiers, collected from the field sensor network and forwarded to IODS.

availability-impact.adjustment-justification: An outage removes sensing at one site; the SOC compensates with guard patrols for several days, so the provisional low value is kept.

information-types.title: ESG configuration and security management data
information-types.description: Device configuration, host firewall rules, account records and cryptographic keys of the gateway.

confidentiality-impact.adjustment-justification: The data includes private keys and firewall rules whose disclosure would let an attacker impersonate a gateway or map the permitted paths into the enclave.

information-types.title: ESG audit records
information-types.description: Sign-in, account change, privilege use, configuration change and update events.

authorization-boundary.description: One gateway appliance per site with its operating system, collector service, admin console and buffer database, plus the field sensor nodes paired with it, authorized as one system across all sites on one configuration baseline. The installation network switch port is the boundary edge. IODS, the installation ICAM service, the installation network enclave and the CSSP are outside the boundary and separately authorized; technician laptops and administrator workstations are installation assets outside the boundary.

network-architecture.description: Each gateway has three interfaces. The uplink port on the enclave VLAN permits outbound TLS 1.3 to IODS, outbound syslog over TLS to the CSSP collector and inbound HTTPS to the console from the installation management VLAN only; the host firewall denies all other traffic in both directions. The maintenance port is disabled unless a technician enables it with the shelter key switch, serves only the console over HTTPS on a link-local address, and has no routing to the uplink. The field radio is an encrypted, paired link to the sensor nodes, which have no IP connectivity. The enclave firewall in front of every site switch enforces the same permitted flows.

data-flow.description: DF-1 sensor node to collector over the paired encrypted radio, unpaired nodes and malformed messages rejected; DF-2 collector to buffer, local on the encrypted data partition; DF-3 collector to IODS over TLS 1.3 with mutual certificate authentication; DF-4 audit records from the gateway to the CSSP SIEM over syslog with TLS; DF-5 administrator workstation to console over HTTPS with sign-in through the identity service; DF-6 console to identity service over TLS with signed assertions; DF-7 on-site technician laptop to console over HTTPS on the maintenance port with local sign-in. DF-3 to DF-6 cross the boundary edge and DF-7 enters through the maintenance port.

components.title: ESG gateway appliance
components.description: Ruggedized fanless appliance with uplink and maintenance Ethernet ports and a field radio module, in a locked alarmed shelter

components.title: Gateway operating system
components.description: Hardened Linux-based OS image with host firewall (deny by default) and local audit daemon

components.title: Sensor collector service
components.description: Receives and validates sensor messages from the field radio, writes them to the buffer and forwards them to IODS

components.title: Admin web console
components.description: HTTPS console for configuration, accounts, diagnostics and update upload

components.title: Local buffer database
components.description: Embedded database holding up to 7 days of telemetry while IODS is unreachable

components.title: Field sensor network
components.description: Up to 40 battery-powered sensor nodes per site and their firmware, paired to the site gateway by radio

components.title: Installation Operations Data Service
components.description: Receives ESG telemetry (IC-1) under an interconnection agreement signed 2026-04-02; separately authorized, ATO to 2029-03-15

components.title: Installation ICAM Service
components.description: Installation identity provider; DoD PKI authentication and account workflow for remote ESG administrators and auditors; covered by the enclave authorization

components.title: Installation Network Enclave
components.description: Enclave firewall, intrusion detection and network access control in front of every ESG; separately authorized

components.title: Installation Cybersecurity Service Provider
components.description: SIEM log collection and correlation, monitoring and incident response for the installation; separately authorized

by-components.description: ESG access control procedures operate under the Component access control policy: the ISSO approves every access request, reviews accounts quarterly and applies the Component policy to the console's local and remote accounts; the ISSM keeps the ESG procedures with the SSP and reviews them with it.

Remote administrator and auditor accounts are requested from and approved by the ISSO, then created, changed and disabled by the Installation ICAM Service account workflow; the console (CMP-WEBUI) maps group claims to the admin and auditor roles. The ISSO reviews the account list against request records quarterly (last 2026-09-12). Gap: the shared local account fieldtech is used by about ten technicians and cannot be tied to an individual; per-technician accounts with smart-card login are planned in release 2.3 (2027-03).

Remote accounts are managed through the automated Installation ICAM Service workflow and its group claims. Local console accounts (fieldtech, esgadmin) are managed by hand by the ISSO; automation of local accounts arrives with the per-technician accounts in release 2.3 (2027-03).

ESG has no temporary accounts. The one emergency account, esgadmin, is sealed in the program office safe and every use is logged and reported to the ISSO, but the console does not disable it automatically after use; the ISSO reseals it and changes its password by hand. Automatic disabling after emergency use is an open item for the ISSM to plan.

Remote accounts are disabled by the Installation ICAM Service on the ISSO's request when users leave, no longer need access or are found in the quarterly review. The shared fieldtech account cannot be disabled for one technician; the team password is changed instead, every 90 days or on departure, until release 2.3 (2027-03).

The console (CMP-WEBUI) and the OS audit daemon (CMP-GW-OS) log account creation, change and privilege use and forward the records to the CSSP SIEM within one minute; the ISSO reviews the weekly ESG report. DT-2 verified account-change events reach the SIEM on 12 of 12 units.

The console (CMP-WEBUI) and the OS audit daemon (CMP-GW-OS) log account creation, change and privilege use and forward the records to the CSSP SIEM within one minute; the ISSO reviews the weekly ESG report. DT-2 verified account-change events reach the SIEM on 12 of 12 units.
The console locks an idle session after 15 minutes and ends it after 60 minutes idle, so users who leave a session open are logged out; users sign out with the Sign out control.

Remote privileged users hold the admin role only through an approved identity-service group claim, and the ISSO reviews the role assignments quarterly. Gap: the on-site privileged role is held through the shared fieldtech account, so privileged technician access is not assigned or monitored per person; release 2.3 (2027-03) brings individual technician accounts.

The only shared account is fieldtech, kept because sites lack a network path to the identity service during some maintenance tasks; it is usable only on the maintenance port, which is enabled by the shelter key switch, and its password changes every 90 days. Individual technicians cannot be distinguished in audit records; per-technician local accounts with smart-card login are planned in release 2.3 (2027-03), and the risk is carried to the POA&M.

The console and OS generate sign-in, account-change and privilege-use events and forward them to the CSSP SIEM within one minute; the CSSP correlates them for atypical use and alerts the ISSO, who also reviews the ESG report weekly.

The console and OS generate sign-in, account-change and privilege-use events and forward them to the CSSP SIEM within one minute; the CSSP correlates them for atypical use and alerts the ISSO, who also reviews the ESG report weekly.

When a remote user is found to pose significant risk, the ISSO asks the Installation ICAM Service to disable the account at once. For a field technician the shared fieldtech password must be changed for the whole team, so individual disabling is not possible until release 2.3 (2027-03).

The console checks the role on every request: auditor is read-only and only admin reaches configuration, account and update functions; users without an approved group claim are refused (DT-2). The OS restricts files and services to their service accounts.

Not applicable: the console offers only role-based access to system-owned configuration and logs.
by-components.remarks: ESG has no user-owned objects to share: access is role-based in the console, and users cannot create or grant access to objects.

by-components.description: The host firewall on CMP-GW-OS denies by default and permits only TLS to IODS, syslog over TLS to the CSSP and HTTPS to the console from the management VLAN, with no routing between the maintenance port, the uplink and the field radio; the collector accepts only messages from paired sensor nodes. The enclave firewall enforces the same flows at the enclave edge. DT-2 port scans confirmed only documented ports answer.

The console separates the admin role (configuration, accounts, updates) from the read-only auditor role held by ISSO staff, so those who review logs and configuration reports do not administer the system.

Each user group gets only the role it needs: SOC operators have no ESG access, auditors are read-only, administrators and technicians hold the admin role; on the OS each service runs under its own unprivileged account.

by-components.description: Five consecutive failed local sign-ins lock the console account for 30 minutes (verified in DT-2); remote sign-ins use DoD PKI through the identity service.
The console shows the DoD standard notice and consent banner before sign-in on both the uplink and the maintenance port, and sign-in requires acknowledging it.
The console allows one session per account; a new sign-in ends the older session.
The console locks a session after 15 minutes of inactivity and requires sign-in again to resume (verified in DT-2).
The lock screen is blank and hides the page content until the user signs in again.
The console ends a session after 60 minutes of inactivity or on sign-out.
Every console page has a Sign out control that ends the session.
When a session ends, the console shows a session-ended message.
Without sign-in the console serves only the banner and sign-in page; the collector accepts messages only from paired sensor nodes, so no other action is possible without identification.
